rules.title: Civil Code section 1950.6 (Application Screening Fees)
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge an application screening fee limited to actual out-of-pocket costs and the reasonable value of time, capped at $30 per applicant (CPI-adjustable). No fee may be charged when no unit is available, and the fee is allowed only if the landlord offers first-qualified-applicant processing or a full refund to unselected applicants; an itemized receipt and credit report copy must be provided and unused amounts returned.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant, adjustable annually for CPI since January 1, 1998
rules.status_basis: Page states section updated Jan. 1, 2026; original enactment and effective dates not stated.

requires.name: residential_rental_applicant
requires.text: when a landlord or their agent receives a request to rent a residential property from an applicant

coverage.summary: Applies to owners of residential rental property and their agents who charge applicants a screening fee.

precedence.text: This section is not intended to preempt any provisions or regulations that govern the collection of deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.

rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.
